source.title: Robust Fine-Tuning of Deep Neural Networks with Hessian-based Generalization Guarantees
source.authors: Hao-Tian Ju; Dong-Yue Li; Hongyang Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The study compares a different Hessian-based measure with empirical fine-tuning generalization errors, testing whether a measured network property tracks the gap.
record.gate_note: The study reports that the Hessian measure correlates with generalization error in Figure 2; the plotted values are not stated numerically. Results cited from prior work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures a Hessian-weighted distance from pretrained initialization and its correlation with fine-tuning loss gaps. It does not measure V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance or test any other supplied version. Its noisy-label experiments compare fine-tuning methods without testing V1's random-label memorization and natural-label generalization comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the generalization-measure results. The authors conclude that incorporating Hessian information into distance from initialization correlates with empirical fine-tuning generalization gaps. They also derive PAC-Bayesian bounds and report improved robustness to noisy labels from consistent-loss reweighting with distance regularization.
record.recipe_differences: Measures a Hessian-based distance from initialization for fine-tuned models, rather than magnitude-aware sharpness based on perturbation tolerance.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported analyses vary model and dataset, fine-tuning regularization method, and, for ViT-Base, distance constraint.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that Hessian-weighted distance from initialization correlates with fine-tuning generalization gaps for ResNet-50, BERT-Base, and ViT-Base across regularization methods or distance constraints.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hessian-weighted distance from pretrained initialization tracks test-minus-training loss in the tested fine-tuning settings.

record.problems: The correlation results are shown in figures without numerical values or stated uncertainty. The tested property is a Hessian-based distance from initialization, not the magnitude-aware sharpness specified by V7.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fixed-random-label fitting alongside natural-label held-out accuracy and chance random-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch, including the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout's effect on held-out error and its dependence on training-set size, configuration, and augmentation.

Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Smaller numerical bounds in Table 6 do not test ranking accuracy.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The paper distinguishes its Hessian measure of average perturbation effects from worst-case sharpness. Neither its perturbation-approximation experiments nor its comparisons of bound magnitudes establish V7. The corrected row states indicate inability to assess the supplied versions, not absence of the reported Hessian-distance correlations.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance.
Large-batch training and its generalization gap.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures; the study measures a different Hessian-based distance from initialization.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Compared the Hessian distance measure with the empirical generalization error across fine-tuning methods.

conditions.value: early stopping, weight decay, label smoothing, Mixup, ℓ2 soft penalty, and ℓ2 projected gradient methods

rows.measure: Relationship between Hessian distance measure and generalization error
rows.note: The authors state that the Hessian measure correlates with empirical generalization errors; individual plotted values are not given.
rows.check: The reported correlation concerns Hessian-weighted distance, not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness. The authors explicitly report the correlation, but it cannot establish a supplied version's effect. This row also combines two datasets that should be separate rows.
